---
title: "Run MatchMiner at your institution"
subtitle: "MatchMiner Genomics and MatchMiner-AI are free to deploy. Here is what each one needs."
---

Both tools run inside your institution's network, so patient data stays there. Pick the one that fits the problem you're solving, or run both.

- **[MatchMiner Genomics](#genomics)** matches patients to precision medicine trials using their sequencing results.
- **[MatchMiner-AI](#matchminer-ai)** matches patients to all open trials using their clinical notes.

[MatchMiner Dashboard](dashboard.qmd) isn't available outside Dana-Farber yet. Its code is due for release in winter 2026–27.

## MatchMiner Genomics {#genomics}

MatchMiner Genomics runs entirely inside your institution's network, so patient data stays under your own security and HIPAA controls. The [documentation](https://matchminer.gitbook.io/matchminer/) walks through a demo setup you can run on a laptop, with example CTML and example patient data.

### Try the demo

You need bash, cURL, git, Docker, and docker-compose. This command downloads and runs the setup script, then serves the demo at `http://localhost:1952`:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://matchminer.org/setup.sh)"
```

You can [read the script](setup.sh) before running it.

### What you need

::: {.req-table}
| | Small instance | Dana-Farber's deployment |
|---|---|---|
| **Compute** | 4 CPUs, 4 GB memory (a laptop) | 45 CPU cores, 128 GB memory |
| **Scale** | Demo data | ~60,000 clinical samples, ~400 trials, ~600 saved filters, ~500 users |
:::

#### Data

The MatchEngine and web interface need two inputs:

- **Structured patient data.** Genomic results and clinical attributes in the [patient data format](https://matchminer.gitbook.io/matchminer/deployment/patient-data).
- **Trial eligibility in CTML.** Each trial's criteria written in [Clinical Trial Markup Language](https://matchminer.gitbook.io/matchminer/deployment/ctml-and-trial-curation).

#### People

We suggest at least two scientists to curate and review CTML documents, and at least one software engineer to build the [data ingestion](https://matchminer.gitbook.io/matchminer/deployment/importing-data) pipelines and connect MatchMiner to institutional systems such as single sign-on.

### Writing trials in CTML

CTML is plain YAML (or JSON), so you can write it in any text editor. Here is one arm of a trial that enrolls adults with EGFR L858R-mutant non-small cell lung cancer:

```yaml
protocol_no: 24-117
nct_id: NCT00000000
treatment_list:
  step:
    - arm:
        - arm_code: A
          arm_description: EGFR L858R, non-small cell lung cancer
          match:
            - and:
                - genomic:
                    hugo_symbol: EGFR
                    protein_change: p.L858R
                    variant_category: Mutation
                - clinical:
                    oncotree_primary_diagnosis: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
                    age_numerical: ">=18"
```

Criteria can combine genomic, clinical, and demographic conditions with `and` / `or`, and CTML can be extended with new criteria. Prefix a value with `!` to exclude it: `variant_category: "!Mutation"` on a second genomic block, for example, keeps out patients who carry a specific variant. Diagnoses follow [OncoTree](https://oncotree.mskcc.org/), so a criterion for non-small cell lung cancer also matches patients with more specific diagnoses underneath it, such as lung adenocarcinoma.

If you'd rather not edit YAML by hand, the CTIMS project at Princess Margaret built an [editor for writing CTML](https://www.ctims.ca).

## MatchMiner-AI {#matchminer-ai}

The inference pipeline is a Python package:

```bash
pip install matchminer-ai
```

### What you need

- **Python 3.12 or later.**
- **A GPU** for the embedding and classification steps. They haven't been tested on CPU and may be very slow.
- **A language model.** The package can run it itself, or connect to a model server you run or choose, through an OpenAI-compatible API.
- **Trials.** One row per trial, with an ID, title, brief summary, and eligibility criteria. The documentation shows how to build this from ClinicalTrials.gov.
- **Patient notes.** One row per clinical note, with a patient ID, the note text, and the note date.

The package is still before version 1 and under active development. Its [documentation](https://dfci.github.io/matchminer-ai-inference) covers requirements, GPU recommendations, installation, and a quickstart with an example notebook, and explains how to choose between local and remote model inference. The models and synthetic training data are on [Hugging Face](open-source.qmd#models-and-data), and the [training code](https://github.com/dfci/matchminer-ai-training) is public. The code is released for non-commercial use under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
